scores.evidence: I've read it as a billing platform sold to many businesses (tenants), each of which bills its own customers

scores.evidence: each module is the only writer of its tables

scores.rationale: Covers timeouts, duplicate/out-of-order webhooks, provider outage without dunning, SSRF, late usage, load shedding, stuck attempts, with detection and recovery.

checklist.evidence: amounts are `bigint` in minor units, with an ISO 4217 `currency` on every money row... rounded half-up to minor units per line
A trigger then rejects any `UPDATE` to lines of a non-draft invoice. Corrections go through credit notes.
stores the raw event (unique on Stripe event ID, so duplicates are dropped)... Idempotency-Key = attempt.id
Hosted pages use Stripe Elements, so card data stays in Stripe iframes... checks the signature
`ENABLE` and `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`... cross-tenant test suite on every PR
unique `(env_id, meter_id, idempotency_key, event_month)`... stored with `late=true` and billed on the next invoice
`next_billing_at` comes from `billing_anchor` using calendar-month addition in UTC, clamped to the anchor day
Starts with `ManualTaxProvider`: tenant-defined rates keyed by country/region, with reverse-charge flagged
default: retry on days 3, 5 and 7; email the customer on each failure; after the last failure set the subscription to `past_due` or `canceled`
pulls the previous day's balance transactions for each connected account, matches them to attempts and refunds, and sends mismatches to an ops queue
Build our own rating/invoicing engine; processors are pluggable | (a) Wrap Stripe Billing; (b) own engine
